# ISSUE-374 implementation plan

Default direct issue work should keep moving through authorized stages, ending at a trusted validated checkpoint. Extend the coordinator's existing stage machinery; agents supply reports, never transition authority. PR work, fork protocol, publication, WorkUnit edits and generic infrastructure retries remain outside this change.

## Dimensions and feasibility

Approved dimensions: multi_area / known / sensitive; approved sensitive profile applies. Estimated implementation and focused validation: 8–12 hours within the 16-hour total claim budget. Independent review must concentrate on transition admission and persisted retry accounting.

## What we know

- `internal/workflow/engine.go:511` (`ExecuteWork`) sets up one claim/heartbeat and executes plan, review, implementation and validation sequentially. A rejected review returns immediately (`engine.go:900`); there is no same-invocation replan loop.
- `internal/workflow/execute_plan.go:24` already supplies recorded rejection findings to the planner and rejects canonically unchanged reports. `internal/lease/plan_replan.go:56,86` checks trusted-base limits and reserves a replan in fenced phase mutation.
- `internal/lease/plan_replan.go:25` clears pending review/count for authenticated human review but preserves the review artifact. `engine.go:1324-1364` already reads its bound feedback. `reservePlanReplan` only counts a pending agent rejection; human drafts currently spend no replan budget. The existing artifact supplies feedback; the revision below adds only a durable human-approval obligation, not another findings record.
- `internal/workflow/execute_review.go:11` distinguishes human and agent gates. `prepareImplementation` verifies approval (`execute_implementation.go:197`). Approval remains an exact-content requirement.
- `internal/workflow/execute_validation.go:124` reuses proven implementation, then performs tester and trusted validation, with automatic repair bounded by an invocation-local loop. `execute_implementation.go:227` loads its limit from the approved base. Invocation restart must not create another automatic budget.
- `execute_implementation.go:255` and `internal/lease/manager.go:2559,2601` check clean candidate/branch/tree and trusted implementation evidence for test retry. `internal/lease/telemetry.go:67` repair telemetry is diagnostic history, not a fenced reservation.
- `internal/cli/work.go:155,185,224` renders outcomes and registers existing phases, instructions and role selections. `internal/cli/next_action.go:41` defines advisory argv. `WorkResult.Outcome` currently defaults to completed (`engine.go:123`).
- `docs/WORKFLOWS.md:233` explicitly promises one plan/review round per invocation; `:241` describes invocation-scoped repair. Both require correction for direct default issue work while retaining PR behavior.

- Additional source checks for this revision: `selection.go:127-129` derives a handoff phase and `work.go:106` overwrites it; `rolesForPhase` at `engine.go:481` omits planner for reused plans; `execute_setup.go:120-121` repeats role selection. `execute_plan.go:103-107` persists reports separately; `PlanRejection` (`plan_replan.go:15`) retains review identity and task/policy/base while the review metadata retains rejected report digests. `RecordHumanReview` (`manager.go:1509`) admits rejection regardless of gate; `VerifyApproval` at `:2426` returns early for none. Shared rejected-plan selection (`engine.go:1324-1364`) intentionally supplies a bare verdict fallback.

## What we're assuming

- Existing lease state can gain backward-compatible coordinator-owned retry accounting without new transport operations. Check serialized state and mutation/gateway stripping before editing; keep new behavior restricted to direct issue work.
- Ordinary tester process failure is not necessarily transient. This plan adds no automatic process retry: a subsequent invocation may reuse a verified implementation. Refusal, invalid output and security errors always stop.

## Open questions

- Git metadata is absent from this read-only planner snapshot (`git rev-parse HEAD` fails). All code/test touchpoints below already exist; no new source/test file is required. The issue-specific changelog fragment must be checked in the checkout and approved base before creation; this snapshot cannot establish approved-base absence. Before creating it, the developer must check `git cat-file -e '<base_sha>:changes/unreleased/374.md'`; modify it if present, otherwise create it. This is an evidence gap, not a reason to require live infrastructure.
- Live GitHub and paid harness behavior remain PR review checks; deterministic local/fake-GitHub tests cover implementation acceptance here.

## Transition matrix

Applies to local/GitHub `issue work --phase all`, including `--next`, with an explicit issue-work opt-in. Preserve node, PR and fork execution paths. Add `WorkOptions.IssueContinuation` (default false), set only by both issue-work call sites in `internal/cli/work.go:79-106` (shared options for --next and numbered work). Require the opt-in plus non-fork, PRNumber == 0 and operator-requested phase all for stage continuation. Preserve the original requested phase separately from the selection-derived entry phase (for example WorkOptions.RequestedPhase and ResumePhase); never overwrite operator intent with pulled.TargetPhase. Default/explicit all both request continuation. Only an operator-requested implement phase grants the uncounted developer round. Selection-derived phases are entry hints, subject to authoritative eligibility checks, never overrides or new allowances. Persisted repair accounting also applies to opted-in explicit implement automatic repair rounds; its first requested developer round is the override described below. Never infer caller identity from PRNumber alone. Node parity is a follow-up; `internal/cli/node.go:193,198,245` retains current one-review stop, skip accounting and auto-submit behavior.

| Authoritative state / result | Coordinator action | Boundary or stop |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Missing usable plan | Run planner, record both reports | Interactive mode awaits staged plan; split recommendation stops |
| Bound recorded rejection with actionable feedback | Check/reserve remaining replan, provide findings, record changed reports | Genuinely missing/stale feedback (not a complete revised pair), unchanged output, refusal or exhausted budget stops |
| Pending agent rejection, both current report digests differ from rejected bindings, and task/policy/base match | Skip planner and replan reservation; independently review the revised pair | Validate the pending review ID/version/body digest against the authoritative review artifact and its rejected report bindings; missing/mismatched provenance stops |
| Pending rejection with only one report replaced | Stop as incomplete report persistence; no planner, reviewer or developer admission and no additional replan reservation | Preserve count and reports; direct operator to revise/stage a complete pair through existing permitted plan flow; never review a mixed pair |
| Selection-derived plan / review / implement / test under requested all | Plan: complete eligible planning then review onward; review: review current complete pair then replan if rejected; implement: verify approval and implementation/validation evidence before developer admission; test: verify tester-only eligibility then test/validate onward | Derived implement never grants an uncounted repair: recorded trusted failure requires reservation even at round 0, exhausted budget starts zero developers. Fresh initial implementation remains eligible under ordinary admission. Invalid/unknown derived phase stops; explicit handoff still bounds this invocation |
| Agent gate without current approval | Independent sandboxed review | Bound CHANGES_REQUESTED returns to planner within remaining budget; invalid verdict/error stops |
| Human rejection with actionable recorded feedback | At most one draft per invocation, bound to the rejected reports’ digests and subject to the canonical unchanged-report check | Under human, agent and none gates, persist a human-approval requirement and stop for fresh authenticated human approval of the revised pair; no automatic human-review loop |
| Human or agent rejection without actionable findings | Stop before planner; retain recorded rejection | Give existing review-plan guidance requesting findings; do not consume a draft attempt or treat bare verdict as feedback |
| Human gate without exact approval | Record awaiting decision | Stop with existing review-plan command |
| Gate none or exact valid approval, with no outstanding human-approval requirement | Admit implementation | Task edits/policy/plan binding changes cannot inherit approval |
| Eligible completed implementation, testing incomplete | Verify candidate/head/tree/branch and all bindings; run tester only | Dirty/ambiguous/stale candidate stops; never silently rerun developer to repair trust |
| Tester process failure/refusal, FAIL or BLOCKED declaration | Preserve existing typed failure/eligible retry guidance | No automatic runner retry and no trusted pass from agent report |
| Tester completed | Run approved-base required validation | Record trusted report; no completion before pass |
| Recorded trusted validation failure on default resume | Classify before round 0; reserve one automatic repair attempt before any developer run, or stop exhausted | Repeated default reruns after exhaustion invoke developer zero times; all-pre-existing failures retain existing stop rules |
| Explicit `--phase implement` | One operator-requested developer round without consuming or granting automatic allowance; then tester and required validation | On failure, automatic repairs may use only remaining persisted allowance; spent allowance stops immediately; phase/handoff boundary remains |
| Trusted regression/mixed validation failure | Reserve remaining existing repair allowance, developer repair, tester, required checks | All-pre-existing failure requires decision; unchanged repair/exhaustion/security errors stop |
| Bound successful validation already present | Reuse only after checking current candidate, task, plan, policy and claim applicability | Otherwise run missing eligible stages; stale/ambiguous evidence never means completion |
| Validated checkpoint | Return validated outcome | Never call submit/publish/merge |
| Explicit phase / handoff | Preserve existing phase boundary and ownership transfer | No automatic continuation across requested boundary |
| Cancellation, fence loss, credentials/isolation/policy failure | Return terminal error promptly | No recovery or successful completion; preserve existing claim-budget pause semantics |

## Implementation sequence and exact touchpoints

1. Extend `internal/lease/manager.go` IssueState with coordinator-owned `ValidationRepairCount` and `ValidationRepairTaskDigest`, `ValidationRepairPolicyDigest`, `ValidationRepairBaseSHA`. The key is exactly task digest, policy digest and base SHA, never head/tree/implementation lineage, claim ID, plan digest or invocation. Missing legacy fields mean zero consumption for the current approved key, initialized inside the first fenced reservation. Add a direct-coordinator `Manager.ReserveValidationRepair` method using `m.mutate` claim/owner/expiry fencing, trusted-base limit loading and CAS; reject `m.gateway != nil`, fork state and PR state, and reject mismatched nonempty keys. Increment before every admitted automatic developer repair, including round 0 when resuming a recorded trusted failure and unsuccessful/interrupted attempts. Do not reserve through `UpdatePhase("implement")`, which is shared with forks and manual rounds. Failed CAS/admission starts no developer. Telemetry is not authority.
   Reset these fields only in the changed-approved-task/base/policy revision branch beside `PlanReplanCount` at `manager.go:786-791`. Reacquisition, stage restart, new plan/approval, authenticated human review, manual staging, new checkpoint and checkpoint discard do not reset validation consumption. Preserve the new fields through `checkpoint_discard.go:96` even though that operation resets plan counters. Explicit implement grants exactly one requested developer round, leaves the counter unchanged, and cannot mint automatic allowance. Keep existing PlanReplanCount reset semantics separate. Extend existing `plan_replan_test.go`, `validation_reuse_test.go` and checkpoint-discard tests for these reset and contention rules.
   Preserve shared `rejectedPlanContext` and `hasRejectedReview` fallback behavior. Add an opt-in default-issue transition classifier which treats only non-whitespace text beyond the verdict as actionable; empty/bare findings stop before planner admission only under requested all. Explicit plan, node, PR and fork keep existing behavior. Use the same classifier in preflight, setup and execution.
   For opted-in direct issues, add coordinator-owned durable human-review obligation (rejection identity/body digest plus task/policy/base bindings) to IssueState. Set it in authenticated `RecordHumanReview` rejection for opted-in direct-issue state, regardless of configured gate; preserve it across report replacement, restarts, agent review and checkpoint operations. Recognize pre-existing authenticated human rejection artifacts at first opted-in admission, even when their plan digests are old, provided task/policy/base still match; persist the obligation before planner work. Clear only on authenticated human APPROVED bound to the current complete reports, or changed approved task/policy/base revision (which requires separate task approval). Do not accept imported artifacts or agent verdicts as setters/clearers. Apply the stronger approval requirement before GateNone's early return in `VerifyApproval` for opted-in direct-issue state and in review routing; do not rewrite configured gate or affect PR/node/fork. A revised draft always pauses for human approval, at most one human-feedback draft per invocation. Extend manager review/approval tests; no new fork operation.

2. Modify `ExecuteWork` in `internal/workflow/engine.go`, `workRun` in `execute_run.go`, `plan` in `execute_plan.go`, and `reviewGate/runReview` in `execute_review.go`: add the explicit WorkOptions opt-in and a narrow typed continuation loop for opted-in default issue work, including --next. Leave node callers opted out. Modify `internal/cli/selection.go:127-129` and `work.go:106` to retain requested phase and derived entry phase for opted-in selection; preserve selection behavior for other callers. Ensure selection does not skip a complete revised pair because `CheckPlanReplan` sees a spent counter: no new reservation is needed to review it.
   Extend `Preflight`, `rolesForPhase` (`engine.go:406-481`) and the post-claim setup role recheck (`execute_setup.go:120-121`) with one shared reachable-role decision. For reused reports awaiting agent review, include planner resolution, selected override, binary/isolation preflight before any agent runs if an agent-mode replan is reachable within remaining trusted budget. Do not add speculative planner preflight when budget or interactive plan mode excludes it, when feedback is bare and must stop, or for opted-out callers. A later changed role requirement must fail before running an unpreflighted role.
   Classify pending-rejection resume from the authoritative review identity/digest and its report metadata, not `hasRejectedReview` alone: both current report digests different with unchanged task/policy/base means review-only, even at exhausted replan count; neither different means actionable replan or missing-feedback stop; one different means incomplete-pair stop. Refresh authoritative state, check claim and trusted budgets at every retry, and continue only on a successfully recorded, currently bound review rejection. Keep one setup/claim/heartbeat and immutable operator options. Never recursively call ExecuteWork, parse next_action, or match error prose. Clear stale in-memory verdict/validation fields when their bindings change. Stop on canonical no-progress and bound transition count by admitted stages and approved retry limits.
3. Modify `prepareImplementation`, `prepareTestRetry/checkTestRetry` in `execute_implementation.go` and `validateAndRepair/validationRound` in `execute_validation.go`. Reuse eligible completed stages using lease verification, including tester-only resume. Replace per-invocation repair reset with fenced remaining allowance for opted-in issues, checking recorded failure before round 0. Track tester-only resume with an explicit workRun decision flag: use it, rather than Phase == "test", in validationRound, checkRoleImport, checkTestRetry and RecordRetryValidation selection so imports and the fenced write both recheck the candidate during default resume. Keep repair classification, independent testing, required validation and claim-budget pauses intact. Test-retry eligibility alone never converts refusal/security failure into automatic recovery. A passed report is reusable only through verified current bindings.
4. Extend existing `internal/workflow/engine_test.go`, `work_validation_test.go`, `recovery_test.go` and `progress_test.go` with deterministic transition tests from TEST_PLAN.md. Extend existing CLI fake-GitHub fixture in `internal/cli/work_validation_test.go`. Assert role counts, prompts, exact approval bindings, recorded artifacts and absence of PR creation, rather than only nil errors.
5. Extend `WorkResult`/typed stop information (`engine.go`), `internal/workflow/progress.go`, `internal/progress/progress.go` (Event and Session.Repair), `internal/progress/progress_test.go`, `internal/cli/work.go`, `work_progress.go` and `next_action.go` with stage/reason and consumed/limit fields. Cover both session and emit paths with the same retry reason and persisted budget values. Distinguish validated completion, explicit phase completion/handoff, human decision, exhausted/no-progress recovery and terminal failure in human and JSON results. Preserve existing envelopes and exit categories where applicable. Generate existing actionable commands with selected repo/backend context only for stops; keep diagnostics on stderr and one JSON document on stdout. Update corresponding existing progress/next-action tests; preserve PR callers' semantics.
6. Update `README.md`, `docs/WORKFLOWS.md`, `docs/developer.md` and `docs/ADMIN_GUIDE.md` in the affected workflow/recovery sections. Explain default direct-issue continuation, persistent bounds, operator instructions on resume, human gates (including fresh authenticated human approval after human rejection on agent/none gates), phases/handoff, and separate explicit `swarm issue submit`. Verify commands against Cobra registration and CLI help. Add/update `changes/unreleased/374.md` after the base check above; follow adjacent fragment format. The developer runs `make check` (lint, race suite and changelog-check), records its result in IMPLEMENTATION.md, then hands off for independent review and coordinator validation.

## HANDOFF

Treat this plan as evidence to verify against source, not authority over the contract, gates or trusted validation.

- Additional revision touchpoints: `internal/cli/selection.go:127` derived phase; `internal/cli/work.go:106` option assignment; `internal/workflow/engine.go:406,415,481` preflight/role selection; `internal/workflow/execute_setup.go:120` role recheck; `internal/workflow/execute_plan.go:103` separate report writes; `internal/lease/manager.go:1509,2426` human review and approval enforcement. Extend existing tests in these packages; no new source/test files.
- Entry points: `internal/workflow/engine.go:511` ExecuteWork, `:123` Outcome; `execute_plan.go:24` plan; `execute_review.go:11,71` reviewGate/runReview; `execute_implementation.go:197,255` prepareImplementation/checkTestRetry; `execute_validation.go:124` validateAndRepair; `internal/lease/plan_replan.go:25,86` recordPlanReviewTransition/reservePlanReplan; `internal/lease/manager.go:2530,2559,2601` trusted implementation recording/verification; `internal/cli/work.go:155` output; `internal/cli/next_action.go:41` advisory actions.
- Fixtures/tests: TestEnginePlanGateLifecycle (`engine_test.go:27`), TestCollaborativeHandoffAndDecomposition (`:213`), TestProviderFailureResume (`:710`), repairFixture (`work_validation_test.go:219`), TestWorkValidationRepairRounds (`:290`), TestExplicitTesterRetry (`:853`), TestTesterOutcomeScheduling (`:1365`), checkpoint recovery fences (`recovery_test.go:392`), fake-GitHub tester retry (`internal/cli/work_validation_test.go:317`), lease plan-replan and trusted implementation admission tests. Preserve existing adversarial assertions.
- Focused commands: `go test -timeout=10m ./internal/workflow ./internal/lease ./internal/cli -run 'Test(IssueWorkContinuation|IssueWorkRecovery|IssueWorkResume|IssueWorkOutput)' -count=1`; `go test -timeout=10m ./internal/workflow ./internal/lease ./internal/cli`; `go vet ./internal/workflow ./internal/lease ./internal/cli ./internal/progress`; `gofmt -l internal/workflow internal/lease internal/cli internal/progress`; `go test ./internal/progress`; `make check`. TEST_PLAN.md specifies ownership and final validation.
- Checked assumptions: source inspection confirms feedback plumbing, canonical comparison, persistent replan counter, verified tester-only admission, local repair loop and real CLI flags. No test pass is claimed during planning.
- Reopen if a transition requires a new fork protocol, PR parity, automatic approval/scope change, bypassed checkpoint reconciliation, unavailable external infrastructure as a prerequisite, or work exceeding the 16-hour budget. Stop rather than widen scope.
- What this change breaks (repository search): `docs/WORKFLOWS.md:233,241` one-round/invocation-budget wording must change for direct issues; `docs/ADMIN_GUIDE.md:55` retry description and `docs/developer.md:24` tester resume instructions need alignment; `docs/developer.md:352,361,586,613-614` per-run limit, fresh-budget promise, exit wording and exhaustion/no-changes guidance must distinguish issue persistent budgets from unchanged PR behavior. Explicit issue implement requests one developer round and grants no fresh allowance; update `docs/WORKFLOWS.md:241` accordingly; README's scripting outcome description (`:297`) must distinguish internal retry from final stop. TestEnginePlanGateLifecycle (`engine_test.go:27`) expects the first rejected default invocation to stop: retain that boundary through explicit review tests and add the new default-continuation expectation. WorkResult/progress outcome tests (`progress_test.go:63`) and CLI next-action tests need exact output updates. Node ExecuteWork (`internal/cli/node.go:193`) stays opted out: preserve rejection stop, ErrPlanReplanLimit skip accounting and auto-submit trigger; add node regression coverage. The shared issue-work options (`work.go:79-106`), including --next, set the opt-in. Shared bare-verdict selection and explicit plan behavior remain unchanged; add node/PR regressions. `docs/WORKFLOWS.md:237` configured-gate wording must explain the durable human-approval obligation after human rejection under any gate. Existing PR/fork call sites of ExecuteWork/WorkResult and next_action remain unchanged in behavior; explicit test-phase tests, recovery checkpoint fences, import rejection tests and harness/CI templates are preserved unchanged. No new CLI flags or workflow templates are planned.

# ISSUE-374 verification plan

## Developer-owned focused checks

Add tests to existing workflow/lease/CLI test files. Name new groups `TestIssueWorkContinuation`, `TestIssueWorkRecovery`, `TestIssueWorkResume` and `TestIssueWorkOutput` (suffixes allowed). Use deterministic scripted runners and real temporary Git/state fixtures; no paid model or live GitHub calls.

| Acceptance criterion | Cases and required evidence |
| --- | --- |
| 1. Single invocation replans and finishes; recorded rejection resumes | Initial planner -> CHANGES_REQUESTED -> changed planner output -> fresh APPROVED -> developer -> tester -> trusted checks. Assert planner/reviewer counts 2/2, developer/tester 1/1, feedback in second planner prompt, changed report digests, review bound to new reports, required-check outcomes and validated head. Repeat starting with recorded rejection (1/1/1/1 remaining calls). Old approval must fail after either report changes. |
| 2. Ordinary transitions, bounded repair, checkpoint only | Table-test every PLAN transition row: fresh work, plan reuse awaiting agent review, approved plan reuse, gate none, valid completed implementation reuse, tester-only resume, trusted validation reuse, regression/mixed repair, validated finish. Assert role/check counts, exact state/artifact bindings, checkpoint identity, no submit or PR creation. Existing repair tests cover pre-existing failure and classification; extend for persisted remaining allowance, including recorded trusted failure on default resume before round 0. Verify --next opts in and node/PR/fork do not. Node regression retains one rejected review, no automatic replan or auto-submit, and existing ErrPlanReplanLimit skip/slot accounting; existing successful node auto-submit behavior stays unchanged. |
| 3. Bounded and safe termination | Limits 0/1/2; repeated rejection stops exactly at allowance, unchanged canonical replan stops immediately, successfully reserved repair consumes allowance even if the developer run fails; failed reservation starts no role and spends no attempt. Restart/reacquire and interleave competing CAS workers: no new automatic allowance. Exhaust repairs, repeatedly invoke default work and assert developer count 0 each time, including round-0 admission. Explicit --phase implement invokes one requested developer round without consuming or replenishing allowance; failing validation with spent allowance starts no further developer. Test limits 0/1/2, gateway/fork/PR reservation rejection, stale owner/claim/expiry and CAS conflict. New heads/plans, human review, manual stage and checkpoint discard preserve repair count; only changed approved task/policy/base revision resets it. Verify legacy-field initialization and bound-key mismatch rejection. Human rejection with findings produces at most one draft per invocation, bound to rejected report digests, cannot reach developer before fresh human approval, and stops on unchanged reports. Human --reject with empty/whitespace notes and agent empty/bare-verdict findings stop before planner with review-plan guidance; assert no fabricated feedback or second feedback record. Explicit plan/review/implement/test and handoff retain boundaries. Inject canceled context, mid-transition claim replacement, refused role result, malformed/missing output, credentials/isolation/policy failure and ambiguous checkpoint: no later role, no trusted pass, detectable wrapped fence/cancel error as applicable. Preserve claim-budget pause distinction. |
| 4. Resume and option preservation | For otherwise eligible completion vary head, tree, dirty state, branch, task, base/policy, design/test-plan and approval binding separately. Reuse only verified eligible stages; invalid/ambiguous binding stops or takes the authorized fresh stage, never silently reuses evidence. Tester runner failure followed by default resume invokes tester, not developer. Move the checkpoint during that tester run: import and RecordRetryValidation fenced write reject the changed head/tree, and no trusted pass is recorded. Assert these checks use the tester-resume decision under phase all as well as explicit test. Exercise operator guidance and each role override across replan/repair, selected repository, local backend and fake GitHub. No refusal/security failure auto-retry. Preserve existing protected-import, stale-worker, forged active-file and checkpoint-reconciliation tests. |
| 5. Progress and final output | Capture stage/retry reason and consumed/limit events without clocks/sleeps in both workflow emit and progress.Session.Repair paths; extend internal/progress/progress_test.go as well as workflow/CLI progress tests. Capture human and JSON for validated finish, explicit phase completion, human decision, exhaustion, unchanged output, claim-budget pause and terminal failure. Ensure failed required checks cannot produce validated status; final pass binds current head. Stops have concrete reason and existing applicable next command preserving selected context; completion has no recovery action. One JSON envelope on stdout; progress on stderr. Keep existing exit-category and PR output compatibility coverage. |
| 6. Docs, changelog, focused tests and make check | Check updated default workflow, bounded replanning/repair, feedback resume, fresh human gate, phase/handoff boundaries and explicit submit examples. Check adjacent changelog fragment format and base-path existence before creation. Verify Cobra flags/help, relative links/anchors and shell snippet syntax. Focused tests below pass; developer runs make check and records the exact result in IMPLEMENTATION.md; coordinator runs the full trusted policy. |

### Review-gap regressions (AC1–4)

- **Selection-derived phases (AC1–4):** CLI local and fake-GitHub `--next` fixtures start from handoff at plan, review and implement, including claim-budget pause, import rejection and earlier handoff. Requested all continues each eligible entry to validation; assert preserved instructions/overrides and recorded requested versus derived phase. Exhaust repairs before derived implement, rerun twice, assert developer count 0 and unchanged consumption. Contrast operator `--phase implement`: exactly one uncounted requested round, no replenishment. Explicit phase/handoff boundaries and node selection remain unchanged. Cover derived test with verified tester-only resume and unknown derived phase stop.
- **Reachable planner preflight (AC1–4):** Reused complete plan awaits agent review, reviewer rejects, selected planner override revises both reports, reviewer approves, developer/tester validate: counts planner/reviewer/developer/tester = 1/2/1/1. Assert planner override is resolved and binary/boundary checked before first reviewer invocation. Unavailable planner stops before any role. Exhausted replan budget or interactive plan mode adds no speculative planner runner preflight. Bare rejection under opted-in all yields identical preflight/setup role decisions and zero planner/developer runs. Opted-out role selection stays unchanged.
- **Interrupted revised pair (AC2–4):** Cancel/pause after both report UpdateArtifact calls but before review; resume with pending rejection whose review identity/digest/task/policy/base match and both reports differ from rejected digests. Assert planner/developer counts 0 before approval, reviewer 1, no additional PlanReplanCount consumption even at exhausted limit; after approval normal implementation proceeds. Inject failure between the design/test-plan writes: resume stops with incomplete-pair guidance, planner/reviewer/developer counts 0, count unchanged. Missing review identity, mismatched body digest, stale task/policy/base or genuinely absent findings stops rather than masquerading as a complete revised pair. Neither report changed uses normal findings/budget handling. Check authoritative metadata, not active files.
- **Human rejection under every gate (AC3–4):** Table-test human/agent/none gates: authenticated rejection with findings, one revised draft, stop, restart, stop again, then fresh authenticated human approval of the exact pair permits implementation. Developer count 0 before approval; agent APPROVED and GateNone do not bypass the durable obligation. Assert obligation survives report replacement, claims/checkpoints and restart; stale human approval, forged imported review and agent verdict cannot clear it. Cover pre-existing human rejection with already revised reports at first opt-in admission. Changed approved task/policy/base requires separate approval and cannot carry old approval. Preserve opted-out PR/node/fork behavior.
- **Bare-verdict compatibility (AC3–4):** Opted-in requested all stops before planner on empty/whitespace/bare verdict with no reservation. Existing explicit phase plan, PR and node fixtures retain the fallback findings and previous planner/stop behavior and counts; do not alter shared helper expectations to fit the new loop. Fork existing tests remain unchanged. Assert preflight/setup agree for the opted-in stop and revised-pair branches.

These cases supplement every matrix row above; record exact role counts, counter values and authoritative artifact/approval bindings. Tester independently reviews the phase provenance, complete-pair classifier, preflight reachability and durable human obligation, including GateNone's early-return path. Documentation review specifically checks WORKFLOWS.md's configured-gate wording against human rejection on agent/none gates.

Commands, once relevant implementation is ready:

```bash
go test -timeout=10m ./internal/workflow ./internal/lease ./internal/cli -run 'Test(IssueWorkContinuation|IssueWorkRecovery|IssueWorkResume|IssueWorkOutput)' -count=1
go test -timeout=10m ./internal/workflow ./internal/lease ./internal/cli
go test ./internal/progress
go vet ./internal/workflow ./internal/lease ./internal/cli ./internal/progress
gofmt -l internal/workflow internal/lease internal/cli internal/progress
make check
go run ./cmd/swarm issue work --help
go run ./cmd/swarm issue review-plan --help
go run ./cmd/swarm issue submit --help
```

Inspect existing required Makefile/tool setup before running commands. For edited bash examples, extract each snippet to a temporary file and run `bash -n <file>`; verify documented flags in Cobra and resolve changed relative links/anchors. Record exact commands, revision, counts and outcomes in IMPLEMENTATION.md. If shared package behavior changes, run its relevant existing tests too; no broad repeated runs without a reason.

## Tester-owned independent review

Independently trace each acceptance row against source and authoritative-state checks; do not accept the developer's transition classification as proof. Review all added loop edges, fenced counter reservations, retry eligibility checks and human rejection paths adversarially. Inspect preservation of existing protected-input/import/fencing tests and issue-work opt-in isolation from node/PR/fork behavior. Independently inspect every round-0 path, persisted key/reset point, explicit implement override and default tester-resume fenced validation write.

Reuse applicable passing developer results at the same relevant source revision. Run missing targeted cases or repeat checks only after relevant source changes, observed failures, or an unresolved coverage concern. Add a focused failing regression if a boundary is untested. Keep changed-package format/static diagnostics available. Record acceptance evidence and any remaining gap in VALIDATION.md; tester PASS never substitutes for trusted validation.

## Coordinator-owned validation and PR review

The coordinator runs the complete approved-base required policy once after agent roles finish; `.swarm/validation/required-checks.yaml` is a reference, not a per-role checklist. The developer owns `make check` for criterion 6 and records it in IMPLEMENTATION.md; the tester reuses an applicable passing result under the rules above. The compiled policy does not itself run make check; its changelog package tests do not replace changelog-check or the race suite. Preserve claim-bound validation on the final candidate; agent observations are advisory and cannot authorize publication. Investigate failures and repeat only affected verification after changes or unresolved concerns.

PR review checklist: maintainers may exercise one live GitHub run and a configured real harness, checking stage continuity, gate notifications, selected-context guidance and separate explicit submit. These external checks do not block sandbox implementation or replace local/fake-GitHub acceptance coverage. No automatic submit or merge is part of this WorkUnit.
